title: Product of a quasi-coherent ideal and a quasi-coherent module: quasi-coherence and sections over affine opens
statement: Let $X$ be a scheme [def-pc-scheme], $\mathcal J\subseteq\mathcal O_X$ a quasi-coherent sheaf of ideals and $\mathcal F$ a quasi-coherent $\mathcal O_X$-module [pqf-def-coherent], [def-weil-sheaf-of-modules-category]. Let $\mathcal J\mathcal F\subseteq\mathcal F$ be the image of the multiplication map $\mathcal J\otimes_{\mathcal O_X}\mathcal F\to\mathcal F$ [def-pur-sheaf-tensor-product], $\mathcal F/\mathcal J\mathcal F$ the cokernel of the inclusion, and $\mathcal J^1=\mathcal J$, $\mathcal J^{n+1}=\mathcal J\cdot\mathcal J^n$. Then: (1) $\mathcal J\mathcal F$ and $\mathcal F/\mathcal J\mathcal F$ are quasi-coherent, and every $\mathcal J^n$ is a quasi-coherent sheaf of ideals; (2) for every affine open $U\subseteq X$, $(\mathcal J\mathcal F)(U)=\mathcal J(U)\cdot\mathcal F(U)$ (the submodule of $\mathcal F(U)$ generated by the products $as$, $a\in\mathcal J(U)$, $s\in\mathcal F(U)$), the map $\mathcal F(U)\to(\mathcal F/\mathcal J\mathcal F)(U)$ is surjective with kernel $\mathcal J(U)\mathcal F(U)$, and $\mathcal J^n(U)=\mathcal J(U)^n$; (3) for every open $V\subseteq X$, $(\mathcal J\mathcal F)|_V=(\mathcal J|_V)(\mathcal F|_V)$ as submodules of $\mathcal F|_V$.

proof.text: For any quasi-coherent module K with a map i to the structure sheaf, form multiplication a = i tensor id followed by the left unitor. The tensor theorem gives quasi-coherence of its source, hence the cokernel and its kernel are quasi-coherent. Transport across Abelian.imageIsoImage to obtain quasi-coherence of idealModuleProduct i M. On an affine open the tensor section map is surjective and multiplication sends a pure tensor to i(s) times t. Tensor induction gives range(a) contained in range(i) times the whole section module; Submodule.smul_le gives the reverse containment by lifting each generator. The affine image theorem and the canonical abelian image/image isomorphism give exactly this range for the product inclusion. Specializing to J.toModulesι and using range_toModulesι_app identifies range(i) with J.ideal U.

proof.text: For any quasi-coherent module K and any map i : K -> O_X, prove quasi-coherence of idealSheafPower i by Nat.twoStepInduction: the zeroth power is the quasi-coherent unit, the first is K, and the next power is idealModuleProduct i with the preceding quasi-coherent power. No monomorphism hypothesis is needed. Specialize this general lemma to J.toModulesι, using the ideal quasi-coherence proved above. For positive section ranges write n = 1 + k and induct on k. The base is range_toModulesι_app. At the next step the power inclusion is the composite of the product inclusion with the preceding power inclusion. LinearMap.range_comp, the product range formula, Submodule.map_smul'', and Submodule.map_top identify its range with I times I^(k+1); Ideal.smul_eq_mul and pow_succ' conclude.

proof.text: For any open immersion j and affine open V in its source, U = j(V) is affine. Restriction identifies the section groups with those on U, with scalar action transported through j.appIso V. The closed affine-extension declaration ideal_comap_appLE identifies (J.comap j).ideal V with Ideal.map of J.ideal U along this isomorphism. Compute the section ranges of both product inclusions using the product formula. Submodule.smul_induction_on in both directions, Ideal.mem_map_iff_of_surjective, and the restriction scalar-action formulas prove their equality. The original and restricted product inclusions are monic: image inclusions are monic and restriction preserves limits (preservesLimitsOfSize_restrictFunctor). Equal ranges on the affine basis imply equal subobjects: composing either inclusion with the other cokernel projection vanishes on affine opens, hence on every open by sheaf separatedness; kernel.lift and the inverse of the abelian image factorization give the two factorizations. Antisymmetry and imageSubobject_mono yield the required equality for j = V.ι.
